metadata.note: The Montour Railroad, a Pittsburgh-area coal road organized 1877 by the Imperial Coal Company (later controlled by Pittsburgh Coal), ran steam passenger locals from October 1879 to 1927: Montour Junction (P&LE, Coraopolis) - Imperial - North Star from 1879, extended over the Mifflin Extension to Longview (Bethel Park) from 1915, plus the Moon Run Division (ex Pittsburgh & Moon Run RR), Groveton - Moon Run, drawn only as a 1915 anchor. Freight continued to 1984; most of the right of way is now the Montour Trail. One operator throughout the passenger era (Montour Railroad Co.), so no Rule 4 ownership split. Research report: research/branches/montour_railroad.txt.
sources: Schaeffer, Gene P., Montour Railroad, Silver Brook Junction Publishing, 1997 (not seen; cited by Sattinger)
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing drawn after 1927. Not drawn as freight-only: the whole road 1928-1984 (every legible Montour entry in the Feb 1952 Official Guide index carries the freight-only dagger), the Library (Snowden) Branch, the Muse Branch, the Westland Branch / Midland Spur and other mine spurs (no passenger evidence), and the 1946-1984 PRR/P&LE and P&LE eras.

not_yet_sourced: Both 1879 and 1927 ends rest on two MRHS secondary writers (Sattinger 2008, Seip 2021) sharing Schaeffer 1997 and the 1987 Craig letter; no 1879-1927 public timetable, Official Guide Montour table or newspaper 'last train' story was read. The month of the 1927 end is unknown.
Moon Run Division: any passenger year other than 1915 [ANCHOR], including whether it lasted to 1927 and whether the P&MR carried passengers before 1912.

properties.speed_source: estimated: no running times were found for the passenger era (research report UNRESOLVED). 25 km/h is a guess for a slow single-track steam local on a coal road with mostly flag stops. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-22), routed with opstrace.py. Every vertex is on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Montour (railway=abandoned, mostly under the Montour Trail cycleway; OSM route relation 2273484), fetched with fetch_operator_ways(regex 'Montour|Moon Run'); ~0.1 mi on an untagged Montour Trail cycleway way. fetch_gap was run over the corridor (OSM trails + OpenHistoricalMap) but the router needed none of it. douglas_peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 11.0 mi vs documented about 12 mi (Sattinger and Seip: '12-mile length'; Fowler table 421: Montour Jct 0.0, Imperial 10.3, North Star 11.9; montourrr.com puts North Star Junction at MP 10.8). No straight-line legs: every vertex is from a Montour-tagged OSM way. Checks along the trace: Enlow 8.81 mi, Imperial 9.47 mi (american-rails.com gives 9.51 mi Montour Jct - Imperial 'per the timetable', i.e. the post-relocation mileage; Fowler's 10.3 is probably the pre-relocation figure). North Star has no OSM or Nominatim location; the feature is cut at trace mile 11.0, between montourrr.com's MP 10.8 and Imperial + Fowler's 1.6 mi (11.07), so the west end is uncertain by about +/-0.3 mi. Montour Junction is drawn at the north end of the tagged grade by the P&LE on the Ohio's south bank (OSM locality 'Montour Junction', 0.0 km off). The P&LE track to Pittsburgh is not drawn (report [10]). LATER ALIGNMENT THAN ITS ERA: the Montour Trail and the tagged OSM grade are the line as rebuilt in the 1920s - Montour Junction - Scott (about 6 mi, 'many relocations of Montour Run') and Cliff Mine - Imperial (new Enlow Tunnel, main raised over US 30) were relocated then (Sattinger 2008; research report [1]). For most of 1879-1927 trains ran on the older alignment along Montour Run, which is largely gone and is NOT drawn. The relocation year is not pinned down, so the drawn geometry should be read as the post-relocation route throughout.

segments.note: Passenger service began in October 1879 with 15 stations on the 12-mile line from the P&LE connection at Montour Junction (Coraopolis) to Imperial and North Star, and U.S. Mail was carried from then (Sattinger 2008 p.1; Seip 2021: coal from June 1879, the P&LE connection four months later, 'Passenger service was then started'). Official Guide entries for 1882, 1884 and 1902 are cited at individual stops by Fowler table 421 (Scott's 1882G note, Ewing's Mills and Jeffreystown 1884, Robb and McClosky 1902G). Steam from the start; no animal-power years. Operator throughout: Montour Railroad Co., owned by Imperial Coal and from 1899 Pittsburgh Coal (stock control did not change the operator). Steam locals connected with P&LE trains to Pittsburgh at Montour Junction; whether any ran through over the P&LE is unresolved. headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE: no timetable for 1879-1914 was read.
sources: Segment-level: start (Oct 1879) from Sattinger 2008 p.1 and Seip 2021, both MRHS secondary writers resting on Schaeffer 1997 and a 1987 letter from the railroad's PR director; Official Guide touchdowns 1882/1884/1902 via Fowler table 421. No primary timetable for these years was read; headway not sourced.

segments.note: From 1915 the trains ran on past North Star over the Mifflin Extension to Longview (see the North Star - Longview feature). In 1915-16 there were 3 trains each way on weekdays and 2 on Sundays, about 9,000 passengers a month in 1916, a Montour Jct - Longview fare of $1.60, and the passenger crews also carried milk (Seip 2021). Over 500,000 passenger-miles in 1924 fell to under a quarter of that by 1926 (Sattinger p.5), and 'in 1927 the decision was made to end passenger service on the Montour' (Seip) as autos, better roads and trucks took the traffic. The month of the last train is unknown. Freight continued until 1984 (not drawn - Rule 1). headway_min 300 is an ESTIMATE from 3 weekday round trips over a working day in 1915-16; other years are unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1915-16 service level from Seip 2021; 1924/1926 traffic and the 1927 end from Sattinger 2008 p.5 and Seip 2021 (MRHS secondary, sharing Schaeffer 1997 and the 1987 Craig letter). No newspaper or Official Guide confirmation of the 1927 end was found; headway is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 29.86 mi vs documented about 30 mi (Fowler table 421: North Star 11.9 to Longview Jct 42.2 = 30.3 mi); whole Montour Jct - Longview trace 40.86 mi vs Fowler 42.2 (-3%). No straight-line legs: every vertex is from a Montour-tagged OSM way except ~0.1 mi of an untagged Montour Trail cycleway way. Checks along the trace (measured from Montour Jct) vs the 1952 Official Guide station table: McAdams 16.62 (16.77), Southview 21.54 (21.84); Library Junction 34.87 vs Fowler 35. Waypoints off the line: McDonald 1.4 km (OSM's village node; the station was at the edge of town), Cowden 0.4 km, Southview 0.3 km, Longview 0.3 km, all others <=0.1 km. West end cut at trace mile 11.0 (North Star, +/-0.3 mi, see the Montour Junction - North Star feature). East end at the end of the Montour-tagged Bethel Park Spur grade near the OSM hamlet 'Longview' (Bethel Park), 0.3 km off. The Mifflin Extension was built 1912-14, so this is broadly its own era's alignment; no later relocation of this section is documented in the report, but the grade was not checked against a 1915 map. Longview - Mifflin Junction is not drawn (report [3], no dated passenger evidence).

segments.note: The Mifflin Extension opened in 1914 (a Pittsburgh Coal memo expected North Star - Salida 'ready for business on or about September 1, 1914'), and 'Operations on this new extension began on February 1, 1915' (Sattinger p.2). Seip: 'In 1915, Montour passenger trains ran between Montour Junction and Longview', 3 each way on weekdays and 2 on Sundays, most stops flag stops, with connections to the PRR Panhandle at McDonald and Primrose, the Wabash-Pittsburgh Terminal at Southview, the PRR Chartiers Branch at Hills, the Pittsburgh Railways Washington interurban in Peters Twp, and the Pittsburgh & Charleroi interurban and West Side Belt at Longview Jct. Drawn from 1915, the first confirmed year (1914 is bracketed but not confirmed). Passenger service ended system-wide in 1927 (Sattinger p.5; Seip), month unknown; freight to 1984 is not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 300 is an ESTIMATE from 3 weekday round trips in 1915-16.
sources: Segment-level: start from Sattinger 2008 p.2 (operations began 1 Feb 1915) and Seip 2021 (1915 trains Montour Jct - Longview); 1927 end from Sattinger p.5 and Seip (MRHS secondary). Station list from Fowler table 421. Headway is an estimate.

Every vertex is on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Montour (railway=abandoned, mostly under the Montour Trail cycleway; OSM route relation 2273484), fetched with fetch_operator_ways(regex 'Montour|Moon Run'); ~0.1 mi on an untagged Montour Trail cycleway way. fetch_gap was run over the corridor (OSM trails + OpenHistoricalMap) but the router needed none of it. douglas_peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 4.96 mi vs documented 4.9 mi (Fowler table 422; Wikipedia 'about 5 miles'). The geometry is the single OSM way tagged old_railway_operator='Pittsburgh and Moon Run Railroad' (way 415684401, railway=abandoned), which carries fixme='very rough alignment' (source: USGS imagery / PennPilot historic air photos / montourrr.com) - so the line is a hand-mapped approximation of the grade, not a surveyed alignment, though not a straight chord. No straight-line legs. Groveton end 0.4 km from OSM's 'Groveton' node, by the P&LE on the Ohio; Moon Run end about 0.9 km west of OSM's 'Moon Run' hamlet node, at the mapped end of the grade (the mine). Any change of alignment over the line's life is unknown.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Seip 2021: in 1915 'The Montour also operated passenger trains between Groveton and Moon Run on its Pittsburgh & Moon Run subsidiary', and 'The Moon Run Division operated three trains on weekdays only' (likely a miners' train). This is the ONLY dated passenger year for the division. Service certainly ran wider both ways - the P&MR (org. 1891, merged into the Montour 1912) owned a passenger car in the 1906 ORER and montourrr.com says it 'had some passenger service' - but no other year is confirmed, so only 1915 is drawn. Do not widen without evidence. The 1927 system-wide end is a ceiling, not a confirmed year for this division; the 1936 end of operation, 1938 abandonment petition and 1939 removal of the rails are freight/abandonment dates, not passenger dates. Drawn in Montour colour because 1915 is in the Montour era; split only if a P&MR-era (pre-1912) passenger year is ever sourced. headway_min 300 is an ESTIMATE from three weekday trains.
sources: Segment-level: the 1915 year and three weekday trains from Seip 2021 only (MRHS secondary). Mileage and stations from Fowler table 422; ORER car listings via montourrr.com are supportive only.
